target_customer: iPhone owners who want a customizable, easy to fit protective case
problem: Phone cases were bulky or hard to fit and not customizable. Graft's Leverage case used a clasp and swappable backplates, including card holder and 3D printable options.
business_model: Hardware accessories sold direct and through retail; frame plus paid backplates ($40 plain or $50 card holder, extra backplates $7 to $30 per TechCrunch)

founders.name: Danny Wen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given.

founders.name: Anthony Ko
founders.background_notes: YC page says 'Sold to Novatel Wireless' and that he now does growth marketing. Named as a founder by TechCrunch (2013-08-19).

founders.name: Peter Szucs
founders.background_notes: YC page spells it Szcus; TechCrunch spells it Szucs.

competitors.name: OtterBox
competitors.what: Market leading rugged phone case maker
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a competitor

technical_complexity.rationale: Industrial design, tooling and manufacturing of a metal latch frame with interchangeable backplates, plus support for 3D printed backplates.

defensibility.rationale: The clasp design was distinctive but the case market was crowded and cases were copyable; no patent was found in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company was reportedly acquired by Novatel Wireless around January 2014 per PitchBook, rather than copied by a case maker.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2013-08-19) reported 45,000 cases sold and talks with retailers, which shows real demand for a differentiated case.

identity.visual_style: Product reviews describe an elegant silver lever and clasp inspired by watch clasps

branding.brand_signature: The Leverage clasp case with swappable backplates
branding.community_and_virality: Reviewed by outlets and a long running MacRumors thread; the company opened design to the 3D printing community and partnered with Zazzle and COLOURlovers for custom backplates.

brand_strength.rationale: The Leverage product name and clasp had enthusiast following (MacRumors thread, reviews), but the Graft name is generic and no brand assets were sourced.

outcome_analysis: Graft Concepts sold 45,000 Leverage cases by August 2013 and joined YC in Summer 2013. The YC page says it was sold to Novatel Wireless and PitchBook lists an acquisition by Inseego dated January 2014, so the end looks like a small acquisition, though the directory marks it Inactive and no price or announcement was found. No failure cause is public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: The acquisition by Novatel Wireless rests on the YC profile line about Anthony Ko plus PitchBook alone; CB Insights lists no acquisition and still shows Seed Alive. Funding conflicts: PitchBook $120K from a16z, DominateFund and YC (August 2013) versus CB Insights $20K over 2 rounds, so the round rests on a single database. Founded 2010 comes from CB Insights only. The directory lists status Inactive, consistent with absorption by an acquirer. No company website was listed.
